source.title: Student Specialization in Deep ReLU Networks With Finite Width and Input Dimension

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains finite-width ReLU students with SGD on fixed teacher outputs and measures specialization, providing related evidence about training outcomes. It does not test CIFAR classification error or most claim-version recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training loss and specialization correlation in experiments; its CIFAR-10 experiment uses a pretrained, then pruned teacher, so it is not from-random-initialization evidence. It also reports that a 1× student can fit the teacher perfectly but gets stuck despite long training. No results are reported for CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or classification training error.
record.test_reason: The study measures teacher-node specialization, regression loss and evaluation accuracy. It does not establish spurious local minima or their frequency, and incomplete specialization does not establish optimization failure. Its width comparisons therefore do not test V2's local-minimum claim; no other version's specified outcome or comparison is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate with one clarification: the specialization guarantees are conditional on sufficiently small per-sample gradients, observation and dataset assumptions, including specified augmentation for the finite-sample two-layer results. They do not prove that SGD reaches those conditions. Experiments demonstrate specialization in synthetic and CIFAR-10 settings, including layers beyond those covered by the deep-network theorem.
record.recipe_differences: Teacher-student regression/specialization experiment rather than training classification networks from random initialization; uses SGD and teacher-output supervision, and reports correlations, loss and evaluation accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Student over-realization and teacher-node strength change specialization; sample size and teacher-aware versus teacher-agnostic augmentation change convergence and evaluation loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Equal-width students are described as getting stuck in teacher-node recovery, while greater student width improves specialization. Figure 5 reports regression losses rounded to 0.00 at every width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater student width improves teacher-node specialization in these finite-width ReLU teacher-student experiments; specialization and low regression loss are distinct outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 evaluation accuracy rises from 79.67% average at 1× width to 83.09% at 2× and 83.85% at 5×, alongside stronger specialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing student width improves specialization and evaluation accuracy in the tested CIFAR-10 teacher-student setup.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The relevant empirical evidence concerns teacher-student learning, not classification error from random initialization. Student initialization is not stated. The 1× claim that the student gets stuck is not accompanied by a resulting error value and appears inconsistent with Figure 5's loss=0.00 title. CIFAR-10 evaluation accuracy appears in the figure, without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. Figure 6 reports training and evaluation loss against sample size, but the supplied flattened figure text does not permit reliable assignment of precise values to conditions; it is therefore not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels, and its dependence on capacity, stopping or regularization.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies under standard initialization, their increase as teacher and student widths grow together, and their reduction after adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks or Fixup.
Initialization comparisons measuring training speed, signal or gradient propagation, or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rise and recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No unrounded Figure 5 losses or verified local-minimum rates are supplied. Failure to recover every teacher node cannot by itself be treated as evidence of a bad local minimum.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping and regularized recipes are not tested. The CIFAR-10 experiment is teacher-student regression/distillation from a pretrained, pruned teacher.
No two-layer teacher-student sweep reports spurious local minima rates as teacher and student widths grow together or tests adding one or two neurons beyond teacher width.
No comparison of plain and residual architectures or depth-dependent training error is reported.
The experiments do not compare initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss-rise-and-recovery, sharpness, or divergence comparison is tested.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization-free Fixup recipe is tested.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss fitting random labels and spurious local minima; the study's own results concern teacher-node specialization rather than testing or using the listed findings.

tranche.reason: The study measures specialization, regression loss and evaluation accuracy. It neither identifies spurious local minima nor measures their frequency, and its results do not test another listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Figure 5 reports loss rounded to 0.00; the accompanying stuck statement does not establish a spurious local minimum. Figure 10 reports evaluation accuracy, and specialization guarantees are conditional on gradient, observation and dataset assumptions.
